title: Curb Ramp, Low–Medium: correct
cause: Why it works: a whole ramp, seen in good light. Box, type and severity all match the label (IoU 0.94).

title: Surface Damage, High: correct
cause: Why it works: large, distinctive damage (broken curb corner with an open cavity), rated High as the rubric requires.

title: Surface Damage: false positive
cause: Likely cause: incomplete labels. A small chip at a curb joint; the same kind of chip elsewhere in this photo is labelled, this one is not. The detection is probably right.

title: Curb Ramp: false positive
cause: Likely cause: look-alike. An intact concrete ramp in front of a shop door. Only ramps with an issue are labelled, and an intact ramp looks much the same.

title: Surface Damage, High: missed
cause: Likely cause: a large area of missing tiles whose exposed base looks like an even dark surface, inside a wide label box. Major damage like this is rare in training.

title: Curb Ramp, Low–Medium: missed
cause: Likely cause: unusual view. The ramp is photographed from very close and fills most of the frame; training ramps are mostly seen whole, from a distance.

title: Curb Ramp: box too small (IoU 0.40)
cause: Likely cause: box extent. The detection covers the damaged ramp, the label also its surroundings. Right defect, but IoU below 0.5 counts as an error.

title: Surface Damage: other extent (IoU 0.16)
cause: Likely cause: box extent. The label marks only the chipped paver edge, the detection the whole damaged paver. The labels draw such damage both ways.

title: High rated Low–Medium (P(High) 0.03)
cause: Likely cause: few examples of this kind. A broken curb end seen from the side; the crop is mostly intact curb and road, and the training data has 142 High crops in all.

title: Low–Medium rated High (P(High) 0.52)
cause: Likely cause: the deliberately low High threshold (0.29). It catches 81% of High defects on validation, at the cost of some uneven Low–Medium surfaces rated High.
